decision.scope: The Verus functional-proof lane at its landed phase-1 scope plus the promoted compose contracts: the committed pin (verus-version.toml: verus 0.2026.11.22.1ce6a59, zip sha256 c955d5958877f4f907cce80aa996d4239a481984829d82e325938c7bf242b0db, rustup toolchain 1.100.0), provisioning in scripts/check-verus-lane.sh (checksum-verified download into ~/.local/share/verus/<release>/, idempotent, pin-checked), one model proof unit (crates/catherine-verus/model/lib.rs: the compose model engine_compose with its gcompose functional spec, the equation-family walk equation_findings with the collected_upto/emission/walk_pos spec mirrors, Lemma A sortedness+validity+completeness and Lemma B key-order/render-order bridging), the parity gate (crates/catherine-verus/parity detached driver over the six-document corpus with the non-vacuity witness gate), the guide tripwire corpus (34 vendored guide examples under the pinned release), the `just verify-verus` recipe, and the nightly `verus` job in .github/workflows/verify.yml. `model_hashes` are plain sha256 digests of the file bytes of the normative files this decision rests on, named in full: docs/verus-lane.md, openspec/changes/add-verus-verification-lane/specs/verus-verification-lane/spec.md, and crates/catherine-verus/model/lib.rs; they are file digests, not canonical-model re-encodings.
decision.rationale: Extend: every phase-1 family is green under the pinned release at negligible marginal cost, and the phase-2 family it funds is already proved in the promoted seed. Executed evidence: the model unit verifies 29 obligations, 0 errors in ~1.5 s under verus 0.2026.11.22.1ce6a59; the parity driver matches `catherine check` exactly on all six corpus documents (5 emissions total, clearing the non-vacuity witness gate); all 34 guide files reproduce their measured outcomes; and the gate demonstrably fires on its fault classes (flipped guide expectation fails with outcome drift; a seeded canonical-order omission in the driver's walk copy reproduces kernel-envelope index misattribution on 05_multi_order.ct.json — kernel EQ 0 …, model EQ 2 … — and fails the parity diff; a corpus stripped to zero emissions fails the non-vacuity gate). The compose proofs ride in the same verified unit, so promoting their contracts into the lane README (the phase-2 family) spends no new proof budget. The lane complements, not duplicates: the Lean twin holds the semantic reference and the 190-document corpus oracle; Kani holds bounded model checking; Verus holds the equation walk's full functional spec plus behavioral parity against the shipped kernel.
proofs: crates/catherine-verus/model/lib.rs under verus 0.2026.11.22.1ce6a59 / rustup 1.100.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu: 29 verified, 0 errors, ~1.5 s wall — contracts: engine_compose panic-freedom with the dense-id invariant (Vec flavor, store.rs:230); gcompose functional-spec equality; equation_findings output equality with collected_upto (out-eq); applicable-emission completeness (complete); per-position emission faithfulness (faithful); walk order equals sorted key order and key_lt equals find_lt (sorted, Lemma B)
defects_found: No kernel defect: after canonical-order mirroring (name-order nids via the kernel's BTreeMaps; equations sorted by (lhs, rhs, rationale, status) per parse/schema.rs), kernel and model agreed on every corpus document and every finding index. The first driver projection assumed document declaration order and misattributed equation indices on multi-equation corpora exactly as a drifted model would — the parity diff caught it before the corpus went green, which is the drift-detection contract working as designed (seeded-fault evidence archived in docs/verus-lane.md).
holes_found: Only the equation family is characterized; keys, coproducts, and pullbacks stay Lean/Kani territory.
The serde parser, the wasm32 surface, and the analysis layer are outside the verified fragment; the model consumes typed values, not documents.
The model's fragment boundary is ROWS_CAP = 8 rows per object; documents beyond it exit 3 at the driver (named boundary, no silent drop).
The guide tripwire pins the toolchain's behavior on upstream examples; it makes no claim about the kernel.
decision.fixture_only_comparison: The parity gate is the fixture-level comparison, wired into every lane run: six documents spanning divergence, agreement, partial tables, zero-row domains, canonical multi-equation ordering, and the proposed→hypothesized label mapping; 5 emissions, kernel and model byte-identical after normalization. What the corpus cannot state — the walk's output equals its functional spec for ALL instances satisfying the preconditions, with sortedness and completeness — is what the 29 Verus obligations establish at spec level (design Decision 4's two-layer answer to the naked-assumption pattern).
